label: GO after consecutive non-reward, last one at S1 (evidence S1 is bad, lean toward a2)
explanation: Fires only at GO; it never fires at D1 or D2. 93% of activation mass comes after an unrewarded previous trial (prev_reward==0), and almost none after a rewarded one. It is strongest when the unrewarded outcome came at S1 (prev_state==1; 75% of mass) and the trial before that was also unrewarded (or lies outside the window). That pattern is accumulating evidence that S1 is bad, and it lines up with the policy choosing a2 (model_act==2 holds 80% of mass). The top windows are GO steps after r0 at S1 where the agent switches to or keeps choosing a2. The predicate uses only observed history. Dev F1 is 0.54 (P 0.60, R 0.49, mass recall 0.70). Plain GO & prev_reward==0 has mass recall 0.93 but precision 0.18. The misses are mostly GO steps after a loss at S2, or at the window start where the history is unknown. Those activations are weak, so the feature looks like a graded read-out of the belief of the agent that S1 is bad / its a2 preference after losses, not a crisp event. I did not directly check what sets the magnitude beyond the quartile coverage, which rises for the predicate cases.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over last trial (GO: a1 S1 u, a2 S1 u, a1 S1 r) and trial before (GO: a1 S1 u, a2 S2 u, a2 S1 u); timing cues that raise it most: phase=GO, phase=GO & ep_dec=8, phase=GO & ep_dec=7.
